entries.core_meaning_english: Subduing/overpowering someone.

variances.meaning_english: He overpowered/subdued the man.
variances.citation: شعر: أُسُودُ هَيْجَا لم تُرَمْ بأَبْسِ (وفي رواية أخرى: وليث غاب لم يرم بأبس)

variances.meaning_english: Any rough/coarse place.
Meaning 'I restrained/confined' (this meaning not found elsewhere in Lisān per footnote).
The thing changed/altered.
variances.citation: قال المتلمّس: ألم ترَ أنّ الجَوْنَ أصبح راسياً ... تُطِيفُ به الأيّامُ لا يَتَأَبَّسُ

entries.notes: Footnote notes this meaning of 'abasta = habasta' is not attested elsewhere in Lisān al-'Arab. A separate footnote adds the word is also said with yā' as 'lā yata'ayyasu', discussed in its own root.

entries.core_meaning: الهمزة والباء والشين ليس بأصلٍ، لأنّ الهمزة فيه مبدلة من هاء.
entries.core_meaning_english: Not a genuine (triliteral) root — the hamza is a substitution for an original hā'.

variances.meaning_english: I gathered/collected the thing (same as 'habashtuhu').
variances.citation: قال ابن دريد

entries.notes: Ibn Faris explicitly denies this is a true root — included for completeness per instructions.

entries.core_meaning: الهمزة والباء والضاد تدلّ على الدهر، وعلى شيءٍ من أرفاغ البطن.
entries.core_meaning_english: Denotes 'time/fate/duration' (dahr) and also something pertaining to the groin/lower-belly folds.

variances.meaning_english: Time/fate/duration; plural ābāḍ.
variances.citation: قال رؤبة: فى حِقْبةٍ عِشْنا بذاك أُبْضا

variances.meaning: حبلٌ يُشدّ به رُسْغ البعير إلى عضُده؛ تقول: أَبَضْتُه.
variances.meaning_english: A rope binding a camel's fetlock to its upper arm; verb 'abadtuhu = I hobbled it.
The inner bend of a camel's knee.
Diminutive of al-ibāḍ (the hobbling rope).
variances.citation: شعر: أقول لصاحبي والليلُ داجٍ ... أُبَيِّضَك السَّيِّدَ لا يَضِيعُ (أي: احفظ إباضك الأسود كي لا يضيع)

variances.meaning: معتقلات بالأُبْض، يقول كأنّها في هذه الحال وفي الحبال أصورة الرِّغام.
variances.meaning_english: Hobbled/bound animals — described as if tethered like wild-cattle in ropes.
variances.citation: قال لبيد: كأنّ مِجانَّها متأبِّضاتٍ ... وفي الأقران أَصْوِرَةُ الرِّغام

entries.notes: Footnote on 'muta'abbidat' notes the original manuscript reading was a corruption ('tahrif') and that Lisān al-'Arab has 'ma'qulat' instead; printed text retains the editor's reading.

entries.core_meaning: الهمزة والباء والطاء أصلٌ واحد، وهو إبط الإنسان أو استعارة في غيره.
entries.core_meaning_english: One core meaning: the human armpit, or a metaphorical extension of it.

variances.meaning_english: Well-known — the armpit.
He carried/placed the thing under his armpit.

variances.meaning: إذا تقلّده؛ لأنه يصير تحت إبطه. وكلّ شيء تقلّدته في موضع السيف فقد تأبّطته.
variances.meaning_english: He slung his sword (belted it), because it ends up under the armpit; extended to anything worn where a sword is worn.
variances.citation: قال ابن دريد؛ ثم قال الهذلي (المتنخل الهذلي) شعرا: شَرِبْتُ بجُمَّةٍ وصَدَرْتُ عنه ... وأبيضَ صارمٍ ذكرٍ إباطي

variances.meaning: قال قوم: أي هو ناحية إباطي. وقال آخرون: هو إباطي، نسبه إلى إبطه ثم خفّفه.
variances.meaning_english: Disputed reading: either 'a direction/side of my armpit' or 'attributed to his armpit', then abbreviated.

variances.meaning: من الرمل، وهو أن ينقطع معظمه ويبقى منه شيء رقيق منبسط متصل بالجَلَد، فينقطع معظمه؛ والجمع الآباط.
variances.meaning_english: Metaphorically: a section of sand-dune where most of it is cut off leaving a thin strip attached to firm ground; plural ābāṭ.
variances.citation: قال ذو الرمّة: وحَزْوَمانةٍ ورقاءَ يجري سرابُها ... بمُنْسَحَّةِ الآباطِ حُدْبٍ ظهورُها

entries.notes: Entry begins near bottom of page 37 (pdf 83) and continues onto page 38 (pdf 84); recorded together since both pages read together. Corrected: the definition of 'ta'abbata sayfahu' is attributed in the text to Ibn Duraid ('qala Ibn Duraid'), not solely to the poetry citation as the prior extraction implied.

entries.core_meaning: الهمزة والباء والقاف يدلّ على إباق العبد، والتشدّد في الأمر.
entries.core_meaning_english: Denotes a slave's fleeing/absconding, and being stringent/severe in a matter.

variances.meaning_english: The slave fled/absconded — verbal noun ibāq / abq.
variances.citation: قال الرَّاجز: أمْسِكْ بُنَيَّكَ عمرُو إنّي آبِقٌ ... بَرِقٌ على أرضِ السَّمالِ آلِقُ

variances.meaning_english: A slave who habitually/frequently absconds.
The man concealed/hid himself.
variances.citation: قال أبو زيد؛ ثم أورد شاهداً من شعر الأعشى (البيت مقطوع في نهاية الصفحة ولم يُستكمل)

entries.notes: Page 38 ends mid-citation ('قال الأعشى:') before the verse itself appears — the poetry line is cut off / continues on the next (unprovided) page.

issues_found: أجّة (page 0055): prior extraction wrote the citation phrase as 'يقال منه اتّقد النهار اتّقادا' — the page actually reads 'يقال منه ائتجّ النهار ائتجاجا' (same root أجّ, not the unrelated وقد root). Fixed.
أحّ entry (page 0055-56): prior extraction omitted the usage 'أحّ أحّاً' (يقال في حكاية الشمال) entirely. Added it.

أحّ entry: prior extraction misattributed the verse 'يكاد من تنحنح وأحّ يحكي سعال الشرق الأبحّ' to the آحّ (ممدود) variant; it actually illustrates the plain أحّ form. The آحّ/ممدود variant is introduced separately, right before the second verse ('كأنّ صوت شخبها الممتاح...'). Restructured the two variances to reflect this.

أخّ entry (page 0056): prior extraction's citation 'قصة رويت بإسناد إلى ابن دريد ضمنا' for the دختنوس anecdote overstated the source attribution — the page states no explicit source for that narrative. Softened citation wording.

أدّ entry (page 0057): prior extraction attributed 'قاله ابن دريد' to the 'أدّت الناقة' variance; on the page this citation grammatically belongs only to the following statement 'والأدّ: القوّة'. Removed the misattributed citation.
أدّ entry: added footnote detail that the الإدد/العضائل verse is attributed to Ru'ba per his diwan (footnote 3 on the page), not left as a bare 'الخليل' citation with no further sourcing.

Root أرّ: reassigned the top-of-page-59 verse ('كأن حبرية...') and its footnote into the second variance (إيقاد النار) as a continuation of the same citation, rather than leaving it only described in notes; also updated printed_page_number to '12-13' since the entry's citation spans both pages.
Root أزّ, first variance ('الأزّ: حمل الإنسان الإنسان على الأمر...'): added missing attribution 'قال الخليل' — present in the source text but omitted in the extraction.
Root أزّ, cold-related variance: corrected transcription typo 'الأزبيز' to 'الأزيز' — the printed text reads الأزيز (per أبو حاتم), not الأزبيز.
Root أزّ, 'شدة السير' variance: added citation 'قال أبو حاتم' (the unattributed 'قال:' in source continues his speech) — previously left blank.
Root أدّ, first variance ('أدّتِ الإبل'): added citation 'قال ابن دريد' which was present in source but left blank in extraction.
Root أذّ, first two variances ('أذَّ يَؤُذُّ أذًّا' and 'شفرة أَذوذ'): added citation 'قال ابن دريد', the attributed source for both, previously left blank.
أك entry: 'يوم أكٌّ، يوم ذو ألٍّ' corrected to 'يوم أكٌّ، يوم ذو أكٍّ' — the page reads أكّ (root-consistent), not ألّ.
أك entry: citation word 'نقظه' corrected to 'نقضه' as printed.

أل entry: the 'سُمّيت الآلة لأنها دقيقة الرأس' etymology had been merged into the earlier 'الحربة آلة للمعانها' variance; these are two separate statements at different points in the text (page 64 vs page 65) and have been split into two variances.
أل entry: the poem citation 'حتى رميتُ بها يئلُّ فَريصُها...' was attached to 'أَلَّ الفرسُ يئِلُّ أَلًّا' but in the text it directly follows and illustrates 'أَلَّتْ فرائصُه'; moved accordingly.
أل entry: 'والجمع الآل / الإلال' corrected to 'والجمع الإلال' — the text gives only one plural (الإلال); 'الآل' was not present.

أل entry: citation under 'الأليل: الأنين' was garbled as '* إنما ربّي تكثر الأليلا *'; corrected to the actual printed hemistich '* إنّما تَرَيْنى تُكثِرى الأليلا *', with the footnoted variant reading (اللسان: إما تراني أشتكي) kept as a separate note rather than conflated into the main citation.

أل entry: printed_page_number simplified to '18' (the entry's starting page); the multi-page span (18-20) is explained in notes instead, to keep the field itself faithful to what is printed on the page.
Entry 1 (أل), variance 'آل السقاء': usage corrected to 'ألّ السقاء' (root verb أَلَّ, no alif-madda) — original had wrong spelling.

Entry 1, same variance: its citation 'قال ابن دريد: قد ختفت العرب الإل' was misattributed — that sentence is a separate, unrelated closing remark (and 'ختفت' is a misreading of 'خفّفت'). Removed as citation for this usage and split into its own new variance ('الإلّ (تخفيف)').
Entry 1, variance 'قول قوم': meaning corrected from 'قرابة الرحم' to the page's actual wording 'قربى الرحم'.
Entry 1, variance 'تفسير المفسرين': citation field was the placeholder string 'Quran quotation' — replaced with the actual Quranic text quoted on the page.
Entry 2 (أم), variance 'لا أمّ له': citation had 'ولقد أمّت أمومة' — corrected to 'ولقد أَمِمْتُ أمومة' per the page (verb أَمِمَ, not أمّ).
Page 72 (pdf_page_index 72): the 'kunā al-dāhiya' list had two misread names — 'أم أزيق' should be 'أم أريق', and 'أم الرئيس' should be 'أم الربيس' — corrected against the page image.

Citation 'قال اللحياني' was attached to the wrong variance ('لا أمّة لبني فلان'); the text actually shows it introduces the next line 'ما أحسن أمّته أي خَلقَته' — moved accordingly.
Garbled/uncertain reading 'الأئمة النقمة(؟)' corrected: the page reads 'قال الخليل: الإمّة النعمة' (al-imma with kasra = 'a favour/blessing'), not 'al-a'imma = vengeance'.

Citation 'قال أبو عبيدة' was misattributed to the variance 'أمامك ترى أثرك'; on the page it actually introduces the proverb 'ومن أمثالهم: رويد تبين ما أمامة من هند' — moved to that entry, and the 'أمامك ترى أثرك' entry's citation removed.
Aʿsha verse quoted with 'لموجوه' — the page shows 'لموجوهِم' (typo fixed).
Minor wording fix: 'الآتي في اللغة المنسوب' corrected to 'الأتيّ في اللغة المنسوب' per Abu 'Ubayd's gloss as printed.
Removed the speculative note flagging the Khalil/Aʿsha phrase as uncertain, since it is now correctly read as 'الإمّة النعمة'.

"الأنانة" variance: original said husbands die on the woman ('التي يموتُ عنها أزواجها'), not that the women die ('يمتن عن أزواجها') as the JSON had it — corrected the Arabic meaning field to match the source (English gloss was already correct).
"أ و" entry citation: corrected 'أَ أَمّةً وآهةً' to 'أَ أَهَّةً وآهةً' matching the printed text.

"أيّ" entry note: corrected — the page states تأيّيت والآية were already covered elsewhere ('ذُكر في بابه'), not that they continue on later pages; added the missing final variance on the page introducing 'آء' (a mamdud plant name) whose citation is cut off at the page bottom.
